about: Results of the AI editorial review for articles published with the automated label. Not a person's review.

entries.notes: Recomputed A², A³ diagonal (2,2,2,0; trace 6 => 1 triangle), K4 trace(A³)=24, C4 A² with node. Definitions checked against MathWorld Adjacency Matrix (connection matrix, zero diagonal, symmetric) and Walk (closed k-walks = trace of A^k); ADS 9.2 checked for the three data structures and edge-list remark. Replaced unsourced road-map/social-network sparsity claims with ADS's own airport estimate (75×4,500/2 = 168,750 vs 4,500², recomputed); dropped ADS's ASCII example because its edge count (3,584) is an arithmetic slip in the source (128·28/2 = 1,792). Replaced non-catalog unit name 'unit 10, Relations, Orders and Graph Theory' with the catalog's graph theory unit.

Definition, n²+3n+4 < 2n² for n>10, 3n+4 is O(n²), 'misused to mean equal to' checked against NIST DADS; Sedgewick & Wayne 1.4 checked (few order-of-growth functions, brute-force 3-sum ~N³/2, faster N² log N method). Recomputed 8n² bound, log2(1000)≈9.97, 2^1000 has 302 digits. Fixed disproof (n = max(k, ⌈c⌉+1) so n is an integer). Replaced unsourced 'people usually mean Θ' and 'better algorithm usually beats faster computer' with NIST's quicksort-vs-supercomputer example; sourced Euclid step bound to MathWorld (Lamé) and added that source. Unit name changed to catalog wording.

All probabilities recomputed (P(X=3)=0.2503, (0.75)^10=0.0563, P(X≥5)=0.0781, P(X≥6)=0.0197, free-throw 0.328/0.737, de Méré 0.518/0.491, C(10,5)/2^10=0.246, sd 1.369). OpenStax Intro Stats 4.3 checked for the three characteristics, μ=np, σ²=npq and Jacob Bernoulli late 1600s; MathWorld for the normal approximation. Cut unsourced 'most important distribution' superlative; removed a non-catalog claim that the app's probability unit covers expectation and variance.

Recomputed (2x−3)^4 coefficients, x^5 coefficient in (x+2)^8 = 448, C(12,6)=924, hockey-stick example, (1.01)^10. Levin 1.2 checked for Pascal's rule and C(12,6) via the triangle; MathWorld Pascal's Triangle for the Fibonacci shallow diagonals. Cut 'the step most often got wrong'; removed non-catalog claim that the app's unit covers pigeonhole and inclusion–exclusion.

Checked MathWorld (bipartite = two-colorable, acyclic graphs bipartite, even-cycle criterion), Levin 4.4 (K2,3 chromatic number 2) and 4.6 (Hall's theorem, Philip Hall 1935, 'avoid the obvious counterexamples' paraphrase). Verified the 6-vertex 2-colouring example and the Hall worker/job matching by hand; exercise answers checked. Cut an unsourced recommendation-systems bullet; unit name changed to catalog wording.

Recomputed the whole table (10: 11.7%, 20: 41.1%, 23: 50.7%, 30: 70.6%, 40: 89.1%, 50: 97.0%, 57: 99.0%, 70: 99.9%), 253 for own-birthday, 253/365, 1.1774√365=22.5, √(2ln2·2^32)≈77,163. MathWorld checked for uniform model, 88/187 for 3/4 sharing, >6% September excess. Corrected a false claim that the e^(−n(n−1)/730) approximation matches the exact answer to two decimals (0.500 vs exact 0.493); removed the unsourced 'most people guess 180' and the 'only slightly' hedge in the FAQ (non-uniformity can only raise the probability); softened the hash-length causal claim.

Majority-function sum of products and simplification verified over all 8 inputs; half-adder and NAND constructions checked. ADS 13.7 checked (Shannon, switching circuits, gates miniaturised, XOR/NAND/NOR notation, simplification example, Exercise 7 XOR); MathWorld Boolean Algebra (bounded distributive complemented lattice, Boolean algebra of sets). Rewrote opening to what ADS actually says instead of an unsourced 'every digital device' claim; cut 'De Morgan used most'; replaced the app's 'Statement Simplifier ... with the laws that justify it' (not in catalog) with catalog tools.

Checked ADS 1.3 (definition, A={1,2,3}, B={4,5} example and the reason for the × symbol) and Levin 0.3 (Cartesian plane as all ordered pairs of reals). Counting examples recomputed. Cut an unsourced SQL CROSS JOIN bullet and the 'most important use' superlative; fixed an FAQ example; replaced 'relations returning in unit 10' (not in catalog) with the catalog's sets, functions and countability unit.

Recomputed C0..C10 and C20 = 6,564,120,420, the reflection count 70−56=14, the convolution for C4, the handshake and stack-sequence answers. MathWorld checked for Euler's polygon division problem, Segner 1761, ballot sequences, Dyck paths, binary bracketings and round-table handshakes; OEIS A000108 saved. Softened 'the best example'; unit references changed to catalog wording.

Verified x≡23 (mod 105) construction table (inverses 2,1,1; 140+63+30=233), sieving, x≡11 (mod 12), exercises (17 mod 20, 88 mod 105, third has no solution). MathWorld CRT checked for the two-moduli statement and general formula; Levin 5.2 for the trial-and-error approach to small congruences. Corrected the RSA bullet and FAQ: the linked RSA article uses the CRT in the proof that decryption works, not as a speed-up (the unsourced optimisation claim was removed). Unit reference changed to catalog wording.

Recomputed P(T)=0.0293, P(F|T)=0.324, counts table, second test 0.958, aces 1/221, dice 1/6. OpenStax 7.9 checked for the opening dice example (3/36, then 1/6 after a 5); MathWorld Bayes for 'conditional probability in terms of its reverse and marginal probabilities'. Cut unsourced 'most common mistake' and 'which is why confirmation tests exist'; removed non-catalog unit contents (sample spaces, Bayes, expectation).

Truth table checked; OpenStax 2.5 checked for the equivalences (contrapositive ≡ conditional, converse ≡ inverse). Softened 'most common mistakes' and 'trips people up'; corrected the FAQ's loose 'negation of and is or' to the De Morgan form; rewrote the app tool description to the catalog's 'converse-inverse-contrapositive helper' (the 'shows which are equivalent' feature is not in the catalog).

Checked ADS 7.2 (countable definition, ℙ×ℙ as a seemingly larger countable set, Cantor's listing 0,1,1/2,2,3,1/3,1/4,2/3,3/2,4 then negatives) and MathWorld (countable = finite or denumerable; diagonal method completely general, power set). Verified the integer enumeration formula and the diagonal construction digits. Cut 'final topic of most courses'; replaced unsourced 'most functions' / halting-problem claim with the cardinality argument itself; unit wording per catalog.

Fixed an error: the summary table paired ¬(p∧q) ≡ ¬p∨¬q with (A∪B)ᶜ = Aᶜ∩Bᶜ; the set column now matches the logic column. Set example recomputed. OpenStax 2.6 checked (De Morgan and Boole as a bridge to computers) and MathWorld (Boolean algebra generality, Venn description). Softened unsourced claims ('constantly', 'nobody thinks', 'standard first exercise', 'most languages'); removed non-catalog app feature ('checker shows the row where two statements differ').

Recomputed D0..D8, probabilities for n=2..10, 720/e, the D5 inclusion–exclusion and recurrence checks, exactly-k and at-least-one variants. MathWorld checked: Montmort formulated it 1708 and solved 1713 (text now says so precisely), Nicholas Bernoulli's inclusion–exclusion solution, close to 1/e for as few as four, 'rencontres numbers' named after rencontres solitaire. Replaced an unsourced description of the rencontres card game with MathWorld's wording; Levin's five-professor nameplate example confirmed; unit wording per catalog.

Re-ran Dijkstra in node on the worked graph (S:0 A:3 B:2 C:8 D:10 T:12), the exercise from A (B1 S3 C5 D7 T9) and with the extra S–T edge; checked the negative-edge and MST-vs-SPT triangles. Sedgewick & Wayne 4.4 checked (nonnegative weights, E log V worst case, Bellman–Ford); MathWorld (shortest-path tree). Removed unsourced 'navigation apps/routers' framing and a claim that ADS treats shortest paths (its optimisation section covers TSP, flows, MST); unit wording per catalog.

Formulas checked against the other sources in this cluster (ADS logic/set laws, Levin P(n,k)=C(n,k)·k!). Fixed the Euler path/circuit line to require connectedness; softened 'cover most problems' and 'best way to revise'. Corrected the app paragraph, which claimed the app 'follows the same ten-unit order as this page' (it does not: the page puts probability before number theory) and 'quizzes by unit' (not in catalog).

Substantial correction. The body described app details taken from store screenshots that are not in the catalog (capitalised unit names such as 'Relations, Orders and Graph Theory', unit-card descriptions, Learn/Practice/Tools/Progress tabs, 'generated and validated questions, no repeats', cumulative/format-specific quizzes, Prerequisite Foundations, tool behaviours, Pomodoro, 12-week grid, level). Rewrote those sections strictly from the catalog (ten units in catalog wording, catalog practice modes, catalog tool list, progress screen per catalog). Also fixed a false source claim: Levin's book does NOT put logic before induction (its order is counting, sequences incl. induction, then logic and proofs) and a misattribution to the interleaving guide (which says interleaving is not spacing). Removed 'most students find' and other unsourced generalisations. Free/ads/no IAP and IQ Test & Brain Training Games name match the catalog.

Checked ADS 6.3 (equality the classic example, behave like equality, equivalent fractions, Theorem 6.3.14 partition with all three properties used) and MathWorld. Verified mod-3 classes, the 14-pair count, the 5 and 15 partition counts (enumerated 1+4+3+6+1). Removed an unsourced programming/hash-table bullet, the unsourced 'Bell numbers' naming and an 'everyday relations often fail' generalisation; replaced 'unit 10, Relations, Orders and Graph Theory' (not in catalog).

Recomputed gcd(1071,462)=21, gcd(252,198)=18, lcm 2,772, Bézout 7·462−3·1071=21, Fibonacci 89/55 nine divisions, gcd(391,299)=23. ADS 11.4 checked (quote about Euclid's time, Bézout's lemma Theorem 11.4.10); MathWorld (Book VII, Lamé's five-times-digits bound, Fibonacci worst case). Cut 'still the method computers use', 'quickest way', 'sizes used in cryptography' and 'most important use'; unit wording per catalog.

Verified the envelope path (A–B–C–D–E–C–A–D–B uses all 8 edges once), Königsberg degrees 5,3,3,3, K5/K4 exercise and the two-bridge answer. ADS 9.4 checked (legend, Eulerian-definition warning, general theorem); Levin 4.5 (odd vertices must be the ends; bridge-builder exercise: one bridge for a path, two for a circuit). Replaced an unsourced snowplough example with OpenStax's delivery-route/Chinese postman framing and added OpenStax 12.6 (Fleury's algorithm) as a source; cut 'the method computers use'; unit wording per catalog.

Recomputed −1/6, 10·0.9^10 = 3.49, 253/365, coupon collector 14.7, fixed-point expectation 1. OpenStax 7.11 checked for the 3.5 die example; MathWorld Expectation Value for linearity. Replaced an unverifiable attribution to MIT 6.042J notes with MathWorld's 'expectation is a linear operator'; softened 'single most useful' and 'usual way'; removed non-catalog unit contents.

Recomputed every modular power in node: 2^10≡1 (11), powers of 3 mod 7, 3^100≡4 (7), 2^2026≡10 (13), 2^340≡1 and 3^340≡56 (341), 561 passing several bases, 7^3≡13 and 13^27≡7 (55), 5^200≡1 (11), 7^6≡12 (13). MathWorld checked (Carmichael numbers, smallest 561; RSA uses factorisation as trapdoor, cracking needs factoring n, p−1/q−1 with large prime factors). Replaced unsourced claims about real key sizes and 'practical primality tests' with what MathWorld says; retitled the security paragraph; unit wording per catalog.

Traced every example (parity, divisible-by-3 incl. 110 and 101, ends-in-01). ADS 14.3 checked (vending machine dispensing gum, parity checker, binary adder, output alphabet); MathWorld (DFA components, NFAs recognise the same regular languages); MIT 6.042J course description (state machines listed among discrete structures). Removed unsourced claims about compilers/text search, 'simplest model of computation', regular expressions and 'which is why languages are parsed with more powerful models'; replaced 'most languages' with the precise cardinality statement; app wording per catalog.

Verified the composition table, f(n)=n+1/g(n)=2n example, 5x−3 inverse, x↦3x mod 7 inverse x↦5x. ADS 7.3 checked: composition theorems are stated with proofs left as exercises (text said 'proves', corrected), inverse example f(1)=2,f(2)=3,f(3)=1. MathWorld bijection definition. Renamed a generic 'Common errors' heading; cut 'most common mistake'; unit wording per catalog.

Recomputed 360 divisors (24), gcd/lcm of 360 and 84 (12, 2,520), Hilbert-style 441 = 9×49 = 21×21, 1,001 and 1,024, gcd(756,1080)=108. MathWorld checked (statement, unique factorization theorem, corollary of Euclid's first theorem); ADS 3.7 (existence of prime factorizations via course-of-values/strong induction); OpenStax 3.1 (statement, factor trees). Minor softening ('usual proof'); unit wording per catalog.

Recomputed the coin-change count (10) and exercise 3 (18) by enumeration; Hanoi partial fractions checked. Levin 5.1 headings checked; MathWorld 'formal power series'. Softened the convergence takeaway to match MathWorld; replaced non-catalog description of the recurrences unit.

Verified the exam timetable colouring edge by edge, wheel exercises, C(6,2)=15 > 10 hint. Levin 4.4 checked (K6, K2,3, 'best known theorem', 633 reducible configurations); MathWorld (clique-number bound, Brooks' theorem); ADS 9.6 (five-colour theorem and degree-5 lemma, now cited correctly instead of 'common exercise'). Removed an unsourced claim that 3-colourability has no known efficient algorithm and the 'scheduling software heuristics' claim; rewrote that section; softened 'for most graphs' in a takeaway; unit wording per catalog.

Verified the C4 bijection, both exercise answers (path mapping 4-2-5-3-1; K3,3 vs prism), 10! = 3,628,800, 4 graphs on 3 vertices. MathWorld checked (definition, no known P algorithm, not shown NP-complete, 'graph isomorphism complete'); OpenStax 12.3 (informal definition, check obvious differences first); Levin 4.1. Cut 'every course tests' and unsourced 'software handles large graphs well'; unit wording per catalog.

Degree sums and exercise answers checked (degree sequences 3,2,2,2,1 construction; 3,3,3,1 impossible). ADS 9.1 checked (simple undirected graph definition, directed graphs first, multigraph definition); Levin 4.1 (handshake lemma wording); MathWorld Handshaking Lemma (name from people and handshakes; odd-degree count even). Cut 'large part of most courses' and softened 'most of a first course'; unit wording per catalog.

Recomputed (n−1)!/2 for n=4,10,20; checked the 3-bit Gray code. ADS 9.4 checked (no simple characterisation, four-vertex connected non-Hamiltonian graph, widely held belief no faster algorithm, a-d conversion Gray code); MathWorld (NP-complete, Petersen among exactly five known connected non-Hamiltonian vertex-transitive graphs; Dirac 1952; Ore). Replaced 'one of the hardest problems in computer science' and 'most famous' superlatives, an unverified claim that MathWorld lists both theorems on the Hamiltonian Cycle page, and an exponential-time claim; added MathWorld Ore's Theorem and OpenStax 12.9 (brute force and nearest neighbour for TSP) as sources; unit wording per catalog.

All tables re-derived. OpenStax 2.2 checked for the dominance of connectives (and/or equal, left to right; conditional; biconditional) and added as a source; OpenStax 2.3/2.4 for row order and the conditional; ADS 3.2 for 1/0 notation (it lists rows in the opposite, binary-counting order, now noted for readers). Removed unsourced 'many computer science texts', 'most textbooks agree', 'most common source of a wrong column' and 'usually first proved'; tool description changed to the catalog's truth-table generator.

Fetched the Dunlosky et al. 2013 abstract (PMID 26173288) since the saved page was a cookie wall: confirmed 10 techniques, high utility for practice testing and distributed practice, moderate for elaborative interrogation, self-explanation and interleaving, low for rereading. Aligned wording ('rated low utility' rather than 'does little'; 'rather than' instead of 'beat'); rewrote the unsourced takeaway that 'most marks are lost' to definitions; checked Levin 3.2's proof subsections. App paragraph rewritten to catalog terms (topic quizzes, review of missed questions, custom homework mode, progress screen).
